title: Targeting Tumor Endothelial Cells by EGCG Using Specific Liposome Delivery System Inhibits Vascular Inflammation and Thrombosis
abstract: Inflammation is one of the hallmarks of cancer and is associated with tumor growth. Tumor endothelial cells (TECs) demonstrate inflamed phenotypes. Endothelial inflammation initiates thrombus formation, which is the second cause of cancer‐related deaths. Epigallocatechin‐3‐O‐gallate (EGCG), a natural compound in green tea, has demonstrated an anti‐inflammatory effect. However, the tumor progression inhibition effect of EGCG by targeting TEC inflammation remains unclear. This study addresses the anti‐tumor effect of EGCG, especially its anti‐inflammatory role in TECs.
